question: Which item out of the following is contained in the concurrent list? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (29/03/2019) Shift 2)
options: Trade Union
Markets and fairs
Tolls
Agriculture
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Trade Union

Explanation:
The Concurrent List (List III) of the Indian Constitution includes subjects on which both the central and state governments can legislate. Trade Union is included in the Concurrent List. The other options: Markets and fairs is in the State List, Tolls is in the State List, and Agriculture is in the State List. Hence, the correct answer is Trade Union.

question: Fundamental Duties of Indian Constitution were taken from - (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (29/03/2019) Shift 2)
options: United Kingdom
Ireland
Netherlands
Russia
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Russia

Explanation:
The Fundamental Duties of the Indian Constitution were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976). These duties were inspired from the constitution of the former Soviet Union (Russia). India has 11 Fundamental Duties listed under Article 51A in Part IV-A of the Constitution. The concept of fundamental duties was borrowed from socialist countries, which emphasize both rights and duties of citizens. This feature reminds citizens of their obligations towards the nation. The duties were incorporated based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. The 42nd Amendment is often called the 'Mini-Constitution' due to its wide-ranging changes.

☛ How many Fundamental Duties are there? → 11
☛ In which Part are Fundamental Duties mentioned? → Part IV-A

question: Which of the following states does NOT have bicameral legislature? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (29/03/2019) Shift 2)
options: Karnataka
Bihar
Uttar Pradesh
Tamilnadu
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Tamilnadu

Explanation:
In India, states with bicameral legislature have a Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) as the upper house. Currently, only 6 states have a bicameral system: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, and Uttar Pradesh. Tamilnadu abolished its Legislative Council in 1986 and has been unicameral since then. Therefore, Tamilnadu does NOT have a bicameral legislature. Karnataka, Bihar, and Uttar Pradesh still have an active Legislative Council.

question: The word ''secular'' was inserted into Constitution of India by the _______ Amendment Act. (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (29/03/2019) Shift 2)
options: 44th
32nd
42nd
34th
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 42nd

Explanation:
The words 'secular' and 'socialist' were inserted into the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976. This amendment was passed during the Emergency period (1975-77) under the government of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. It changed the description of India from 'Sovereign Democratic Republic' to 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic' and also replaced 'unity of the Nation' with 'unity and integrity of the Nation'. The 42nd Amendment is often called the 'Mini-Constitution' due to its extensive changes, which included alterations to Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles, and the powers of the judiciary and executive. It is one of the most significant amendments in Indian constitutional history.

☛ Which word was added along with 'secular' in the Preamble? → Socialist
☛ Under which Prime Minister was the 42nd Amendment passed? → Indira Gandhi
☛ What is the 42nd Amendment commonly called? → Mini-Constitution
☛ How many times has the Preamble been amended? → Once (by the 42nd Amendment)

question: With which of the following is Mandal Commission report associated?  (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (29/03/2019) Shift 3)
options: Economic reforms
Panchayati Raj
Human rights
Backward classes
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Backward classes

Explanation:

question: Through which Constitutional Amendment was the Nagarpalika Bill passed?  (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (29/03/2019) Shift 3)
options: 73
74
70
72
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 74

Explanation:
The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 grants constitutional status to municipalities in India. This amendment added Part IX-A (Articles 243-P to 243-ZG) to the Constitution. It was enacted to strengthen urban local self-government. The amendment provides for the constitution of Nagar Nigams (for metropolitan areas), Nagar Palikas (for smaller cities), and Nagar Panchayats (for transitional areas). The 74th Amendment sets rules for municipal elections, tenure, ward committees, and financial powers. In contrast, the 73rd Amendment relates to Panchayati Raj institutions. The 70th and 72nd Amendments deal with other subjects. Hence, the Nagarpalika Bill was passed through the 74th Amendment.

☛ Which amendment relates to Panchayati Raj? → 73rd Amendment
☛ What is the year of the 74th Amendment? → 1992
☛ Which part was added by the 74th Amendment? → Part IX-A (Articles 243-P to 243-ZG)
☛ Articles 243-P in 74th Amendment deal with? → Definitions and types of municipalities

question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (29/03/2019) Shift 3)
options: Right against exploitation
Right to constitution remedies
Cultural and educational rights
Right to property
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Right to property.

Explanation:
The Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution (Articles 12-35) include Right against exploitation (Articles 23-24), Right to constitutional remedies (Article 32), and Cultural and educational rights (Articles 29-30). The Right to property was originally a Fundamental Right under Article 31, but the 44th Constitutional Amendment (1978) removed it from the list of Fundamental Rights and made it a constitutional right under Article 300A. Therefore, the Right to property is not a Fundamental Right currently; it is a legal right. Other options are all Fundamental Rights.

question: What is the retirement age of the Supreme Court Judges? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (30/03/2019) Shift 1)

70 years
60 years
75 years
solution:

Explanation:

question: Which of the following Articles of our constitution deals with the special status of Jammu and Kashmir? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (30/03/2019) Shift 1)

It was added to the constitution on October 17, 1949, and allowed the state to have its own constitution and separate laws compared to other Indian states. Article 370 was a temporary provision in Part XXI of the Constitution and was a subject of debate until its abrogation.

question: The Union State List of Indian Constitution was taken from -  (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (30/03/2019) Shift 2)
options: United States of America
Canada
Netherlands

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Canada

Explanation:
The Union State List (also known as the Concurrent List) of the Indian Constitution was adopted from the Canadian Constitution. In Canada, there is a clear division of legislative powers between federal and provincial governments, including a concurrent list. The framers of the Indian Constitution borrowed this concept to reduce conflicts between the centre and states. This list allows both the union and state governments to legislate on certain subjects like education, forests, and labour welfare. The system is crucial for maintaining balance between the union list and state list. Apart from Canada, India borrowed the parliamentary system from Britain, fundamental rights from the USA, and directive principles of state policy from Ireland.

question: Who appoints the Judges of the High Court? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (30/03/2019) Shift 2)

question: The President's rule in a state means that the state is ruled by- (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (30/03/2019) Shift 3)

question: The five year term of the President is calculated from the- (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (30/03/2019) Shift 3)
options: Next day of his election result
Day he assumes charge
Date of his election result
First day of the month he assumes charge
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Day he assumes charge

Explanation:
According to Article 56 of the Indian Constitution, the President's term of office is five years, calculated from the date he assumes charge, not from the date of election result or the next day. This provision ensures a clear and unambiguous start of the term. The President is elected by the Electoral College and begins his duties only after taking the oath. The term calculation begins from this date. If a new President is not elected by the end of the term, the incumbent continues in office until the successor assumes charge. This rule maintains continuity in the highest office of the country. The President's term is fixed, but he can resign earlier by addressing the Vice President. Impeachment for violation of the Constitution is also a provision for removal before the term ends.

It is famous for its beaches and tourism. The other options: Sikkim became the 22nd state in 1975, Mizoram became the 23rd state in 1987, and Arunachal Pradesh became the 24th state in 1987.

question_hi: राज्य का दर्जा हासिल करने वाला 25वां भारतीय राज्य कौन-सा है ? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (31/03/2019) Shift 1)
options_hi: सिक्किम
गोवा
अरुणाचल प्रदेश
मिज़ोरम
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है गोवा

Explanation:
भारत के 28 राज्यों में से गोवा 25वां राज्य बना। इसे 30 मई 1987 को पूर्ण राज्य का दर्जा दिया गया। गोवा पहले पुर्तगाली उपनिवेश था और 1961 में भारत में विलय हुआ। 1987 तक यह केंद्र शासित प्रदेश था। राज्य बनने के बाद इसे भारत का 25वां राज्य घोषित किया गया। गोवा भारत का सबसे छोटा राज्य है (क्षेत्रफल की दृष्टि से) और पश्चिमी तट पर स्थित है। यह अपने समुद्र तटों और पर्यटन के लिए प्रसिद्ध है।
